name: Maacah (King of Maacah, an Aramean petty king hired by the Ammonites against David)
title: Aramean petty king
summary: The King of Maacah was an Aramean petty king who ruled a small kingdom north of Israel, in the region of the Golan Heights. He was hired as a mercenary by the Ammonites along with other Aramean forces to fight against King David. His forces were defeated by David's commander Joab in a decisive battle.

keyEvents.title: The Ammonites hire Aramean forces
keyEvents.description: After the Ammonite king Hanun had dishonored David's envoys, the Ammonites hired the king of Maacah along with the Arameans from Beth-Rehob and Zobah, as well as men from Tob, to fight against David.

keyEvents.title: Joab meets the enemy in battle
keyEvents.description: David's commander Joab organized Israel's army into two divisions to face the threat from the Ammonites ahead of him and the Arameans, including Maacah's men, behind him.

keyEvents.title: The defeat of the Arameans
keyEvents.description: The Arameans, including the forces of the king of Maakah, fled when Joab advanced against them, and the Ammonites withdrew to their city.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: 1 Chronicles also tells how the Ammonites hired the king of Maakah and his people with a thousand men, along with other Aramean forces, to fight against Israel.

keyEvents.title: Joab's victory described in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Also in the account in Chronicles, it is described how Joab defeated the Arameans, including the men of Maakah, and put them to flight.
